Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; may I ask how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

Additionally, have you noticed any specific patterns, such as the rash appearing after exposure to sunlight, new clothing, or contact with plants or animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica (PLC)

Thank you for the details. While the chronic, pruritic nature of the rash on your upper extremities is consistent with PLC, I need to rule out other differentials like subacute cutaneous lupus or drug eruptions. Can you describe the appearance of the lesions in more detail—are they small papules, scaly patches, or vesicles? Also, do you have any joint pain or fever?
